text.p: Headlines from major national newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
EL PAIS
- Prime Minister Jose Maria Aznar said there were "points of disagreement" in his meeting with Catalan CiU leader Pujol.
- Writer and reporter Luis Cebrian is since yesterday a member of the "Academia de La lengua".
- Jose Antonio Perote, brother of former secret services' chief, told judge Garzon he would have Cesid papers two months earlier.
EL MUNDO
- Hard liners of the Basque ETA separatist movement criticise HB leaders for paying bail and freeing prisoners.
ABC
- All TV operators could offer Pay Per View soccer
CINCO DIAS
- Rato asks banks to reduce profits.
- Labour reform pact effective from today - firms can offer contracts with lower social contributions and dismissals 33 days
- Cars sold via Internet is warning to regular car dealers.
- Air Europa in deals with three companies to extend its business in America.
EXPANSION
- Prime Minister Aznar asks for low wage increases to reach a (1997) inflation rate of 2.2 percent.
- The government to liberalise land.
- Former Bank of Spain's governor expects Europe's single currency to accelerate banking sector consolidation with mergers.
GACETA DE LOS NEGOCIOS
- The government reduced 1997 inflation goal to 2.2 percent.
- State holding SEPI likes American Airlines as potential buyer of part of Iberia's stake in Aerolineas Argentina.
- The government will create a water market to finance big infrastuctures.
- Banks in fight for football clubs being listed.
- Spanish hypermarket chain Pryca will try to avoid restriction in the concession of licenses for supermarkets.
